The neighbours are going away for the season and their garden will
stand empty. They offered the plot to us on the same terms as last
year: we till, we water, we share the tomatoes at the end.

Their soil is heavier than ours, which is good for the squash and
miserable for the carrots. Plan the rows accordingly. They asked
specifically about the rosemary — it needs the chalk bed near the
south wall, not the clay.

Reminder to self: the deal includes the garden gate key, which lives
under the third slate, and they are particular about the compost
bins being turned once a week.
